deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 17% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.9% = 10-year Treasury 4.9% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 20% last year; 19%/yr over 3 years — roughly in line with its recent growth.

deeper.text: Not meaningful (the company holds more cash than its debt plus equity, or data is missing); return on shareholders' equity 18% (3 years ago 12%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $669M, up 17% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Earnings-quality red flags
flags: Receivables (money customers still owe) up 37% vs quarterly sales up 22% (days to collect 46 → 51). Customers may be paying more slowly, or sales were pulled forward.

deeper.title: Multi-year view

tiles.title: Earnings per share
tiles.sub: +25% vs a year ago · $8.41 over 12 months (GAAP)
tiles.read: Profit per share grew 25%, in step with sales (22%) (latest quarter vs a year earlier): growth comes from more business, not cost cuts.
tiles.explain: EPS = profit divided by the number of shares. The quarterly figures are the 'adjusted' EPS analysts track (Yahoo); the 12-month figure is the official GAAP number from SEC filings.

tiles.title: Earnings vs forecasts
tiles.sub: last 8 reports · bars = EPS beat (+) or miss (−) vs the average forecast
tiles.read: Beat forecasts 8 quarters running by about 14%, yet the stock fell after 5 of them: beats are already expected.
tiles.explain: A 'beat' means reported EPS came in above the average analyst forecast. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

tiles.title: Sales growth
tiles.sub: latest quarter +22% vs a year earlier · 12-month sales $11.6B
tiles.read: Latest quarter: sales up 22% vs a year earlier, about as fast as two quarters ago (23%): steady demand.
tiles.explain: Headline: sales over the last 12 months vs the 12 months before. Bars: each quarter's sales vs the same quarter a year earlier.

tiles.title: Profit margins
tiles.read: Each $100 of sales leaves $28 of operating profit, about the same as a year ago.
tiles.explain: Operating margin = operating profit ÷ sales. Gross margin = what's left after the direct cost of the product.

tiles.title: Free cash flow
tiles.read: It turned 122% of its reported profit into spare cash: the profits are real money, not just accounting.
tiles.explain: Free cash flow = cash from operations minus spending on equipment and buildings: money the company could return or reinvest.

tiles.title: Price vs profits (P/E)
tiles.read: You pay 53× last year's profit (lower than 82% of the last 5 years); only 36× next year's forecast, so the market expects profits to jump.
tiles.explain: P/E = share price ÷ earnings per share. Forward P/E uses next year's forecast earnings.

tiles.title: Next earnings
tiles.read: Reports Jan 21; analysts expect EPS of $2.95, up 17% from a year ago. It usually moves about 6% the day after, so expect a swing.
tiles.explain: Consensus = the average analyst forecast (Yahoo, unofficial). The typical move is the average size of the stock's next-day move after its last reports, not an options-implied figure.

tiles.title: Company outlook
tiles.read: No numeric outlook was found in the latest earnings release, so the next report carries more surprise risk.
tiles.explain: Guidance = what management says it expects for the next quarter or year, from its 8-K earnings release.

tiles.title: Forecast changes
tiles.read: Next year's EPS forecast is up 3% in 90 days (24 raised, 1 cut lately): forecasts are edging up.
tiles.explain: How the average analyst forecast for next year's earnings per share changed (Yahoo, unofficial).
